bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Support acts as an invisible price floor beneath the market that cushions falling prices and pushes price action higher, while resistance serves as an invisible price ceiling above the market that blocks rising prices and pushes price action lower.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Support (The Floor): An invisible price boundary beneath the market... Resistance (The Ceiling): An invisible price barrier above the market.

facts.statement: Price congestion, or consolidation, is a period of sideways price action oscillating within a defined channel bounded by a floor of support and a ceiling of resistance before a decisive market breakout occurs.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Price Congestion (Consolidation): A period of sideways price action oscillating within a defined channel bounded by a floor of support and a ceiling of resistance.

facts.statement: An isolated pivot high is a three-bar pattern where the center candle posts a higher high and higher low than adjacent bars defining a ceiling, whereas an isolated pivot low posts lower lows and highs defining a floor.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Isolated Pivot High: A three-bar reversal pattern where the center candle posts both a higher high and a higher low... defining the initial ceiling.

facts.statement: Clear water represents a clearly visible gap between the closing price of a breakout candle and the support or resistance line being breached, signaling a true trend breakout rather than a minor intraday price spike.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Clear Water: A clearly visible gap between the closing price of a breakout candle and the support/resistance line being breached, signaling a true breakout.

facts.statement: A fake out is a false breakout past support or resistance occurring on low volume, engineered by market insiders to trap retail traders on the wrong side of the market before reversing sharply.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Fake Out: A false breakout past support or resistance occurring on low volume, manipulated by market insiders to trap retail traders.

facts.statement: Financial markets spend approximately 70 percent of their time moving sideways building cause in consolidation channels and only 30 percent of their time moving in active, directional price trends.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The 70/30 Consolidation-to-Trend Ratio: Market Time approx 70% Sideways (Consolidation) + 30% Trending.

facts.statement: Sideways price congestion is generated by three primary market drivers: pending fundamental news releases, insider accumulation or distribution campaigns, and old historical price barriers trapping weak market participants.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Three Causes of Sideways Movement: Fundamental News, Insider Operations, Old Price Barriers.

facts.statement: A valid market breakout requires a decisive candle close past the S/R barrier with clear water combined with well-above-average, rising volume to reflect the institutional effort needed to escape congestion.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Valid Breakout Formula: Valid Breakout = Clear Water Close + High / Rising Volume.

facts.statement: Following a breakout, a valid price pullback or re-test toward the broken support or resistance level must occur on low or falling volume to confirm trend continuation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Valid Pullback Re-test Rule: Valid Re-test = Price Pullback to Broken Level + Low / Falling Volume.

facts.statement: Coulling compares price structures to a multi-story house where a broken ceiling (resistance) becomes the floor of support for the next level up, and a broken floor becomes a ceiling of resistance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The analogy that I always use to explain this type of price action is that of a house, with floors and ceilings... Resistance Turns to Support... Support Turns to Resistance.

facts.statement: Support and resistance boundaries are not rigid rods of steel but flexible rubber bands with elastic give, meaning minor price ticks beyond a line do not constitute a breakout without volume confirmation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The 'Rubber Band' Rule: Support and resistance lines are not rigid rods of steel; they are flexible, elastic bands with 'give'.

facts.statement: Support and resistance zones represent dense populations of trapped buyers and sellers whose psychological shifts from greed to fear turn historical price levels into self-fulfilling price barriers.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Psychological Mechanics: Support and resistance zones represent dense populations of trapped buyers and sellers whose fear and greed turn historical price levels into self-fulfilling price barriers.

facts.statement: Breaking away from a congested price zone requires massive effort and rising volume, acting similarly to pulling a heavy object out of deep quicksand or a sticky bog.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Quicksand / Bog: Breaking away from a congested price zone requires massive effort and rising volume, like pulling a heavy object out of quicksand.

facts.statement: Price congestion areas act as the natural spawning grounds where new primary, secondary, or minor market trends are born following extended periods of cause-building.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Spawning Grounds: Price congestion areas act as the natural spawning grounds where new trends are born.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
